summary: We compute 1! − 2! + 3! − 4! + … ± N!. The factorial is built step by step (`fact *= k`) instead of from scratch, and the sign depends on whether k is odd or even (T1 — simple loop).

blocks.title: Read N
blocks.text: Copy the long prompt exactly: `Enter a positive integer N: `.

blocks.title: Start the total and the factorial
blocks.text: `fact = 1` is 0!, the starting point for building 1!, 2!, 3!, … by multiplication.

blocks.title: Build k! from (k−1)!
blocks.text: Multiplying the previous factorial by k gives the next one in a single step. Recomputing each factorial with its own loop also works, but it is more code.

blocks.title: Add odd terms, subtract even terms
blocks.text: 1!, 3!, 5!, … are added and 2!, 4!, … are subtracted, so `k % 2 == 1` picks the sign. The answer can be negative and very large (N = 20 → about −2.3 × 10¹⁸), which Python ints handle.

blocks.title: Print the answer
blocks.text: Exact format: `The alternating factorial sum is: -19`.

pitfalls: Starting `fact` at 0 — every product would be 0.
